claims.claim: The HC3 annotators summarised that ChatGPT writes in an organised manner with clear logic.
claims.source: Guo, Zhang, Wang, Jiang, Nie, Ding, Yue & Wu, 'How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts?' (HC3), 2023
claims.quote: ChatGPT writes in an organized manner, with clear logic
claims.page: Section 3, Distinctive Patterns of ChatGPT, item (a)

claims.claim: The same summary describes ChatGPT as defining the core concept, answering step by step and offering a summary at the end, following a deduction and summary structure.
claims.quote: following the deduction and summary structure
claims.page: Section 3, Distinctive Patterns of ChatGPT, item (a)

claims.claim: The HC3 annotators reported that ChatGPT expresses less emotion in its responses than human answerers.
claims.quote: ChatGPT expresses less emotion in its responses
claims.page: Section 3, Major Differences between Human and ChatGPT, item (d)

claims.claim: Jentzsch and Kersting measured that over ninety percent of one thousand and eight generated jokes were the same twenty-five jokes.
claims.source: Jentzsch & Kersting, German Aerospace Center and TU Darmstadt, 2023
claims.quote: Over 90% of 1008 generated jokes were the same 25 Jokes

claims.claim: Naous and colleagues showed that multilingual and Arabic monolingual language models exhibit bias towards entities associated with Western culture.
claims.source: Naous, Ryan, Ritter & Xu, Georgia Institute of Technology, CAMeL, 2024
claims.quote: exhibit bias towards entities associated with Western culture

claims.claim: Mohammadi found that RLHF-aligned models exhibit lower entropy in token predictions than their base counterparts in the Llama-2 series.
claims.source: Behnam Mohammadi, Carnegie Mellon Tepper School of Business, 'Creativity Has Left the Chat', 2024
claims.quote: aligned models exhibit lower entropy in token predictions

claims.claim: The same paper reports that aligned models gravitate towards attractor states, indicating limited output diversity.
claims.quote: gravitate towards "attractor states", indicating limited output diversity

claims.claim: Yakura and colleagues measured that words preferentially generated by ChatGPT, among them delve, showcase, boast, intricacies and meticulous, increased abruptly in spontaneous human speech.
claims.source: Yakura, Lopez-Lopez, Brinkmann et al., Max Planck Institute for Human Development, 2024
claims.quote: increased abruptly in spontaneous human speech

claims.claim: The synthetic-control analysis behind that finding covered 737,083 hours of conversation from 824,634 podcast episodes.
claims.source: Yakura et al., Max Planck Institute for Human Development, 2024
claims.quote: 737,083 hours of conversation from 824,634 podcast episodes

claims.claim: Huang and colleagues simulated Wikipedia revision with GPT-4o-mini and Gemini-1.5-Flash and found that the models substantially reduce the use of auxiliary verbs.
claims.source: Huang, Xu, Geng, Wan & Chen, 'Wikipedia in the Era of LLMs: Evolution and Risks', Transactions on Machine Learning Research, February 2026
claims.quote: LLMs substantially reduce the use of auxiliary verbs
claims.page: Section 4.2, Direct Impact 2: Linguistic Style, Results

claims.claim: In that study's summary table, LLM processing of Wikipedia articles raised the noun rate, the long-word rate and the average syllables per word while lowering the one-syllable word rate.
claims.source: Huang et al., TMLR, February 2026, Table 1 (Summary of linguistic style trends)

claims.claim: The same table records that LLM processing of Wikipedia articles raised the average sentence length, the long-sentence rate, the average parse tree depth and the clause rate.
claims.source: Huang et al., TMLR, February 2026, Table 1

claims.claim: The same table records that LLM processing lowered the passive-voice rate in Wikipedia articles while the real Wikipedia trend over the same period rose, so that one metric did not corroborate the simulation.
claims.source: Huang et al., TMLR, February 2026, Table 1 and Section 4.2 Results

claims.claim: Triedman and Mantzarlis conclude that sourcing guardrails have largely been lifted on Grokipedia.
claims.source: Harold Triedman & Alexios Mantzarlis, Cornell Tech, 'What did Elon change? A comprehensive analysis of Grokipedia', November 2025
claims.quote: sourcing guardrails have largely been lifted on Grokipedia

claims.claim: The same analysis found that Grokipedia articles are much longer and more verbose than Wikipedia articles and cite twice as many sources.
claims.quote: Grokipedia articles are much longer and more verbose than Wikipedia
